pointers.sentence: Neither constructor calls the base one, and a comment in the base's `__init__` warns that each assignment made there should be made in `WSGIRequest.__init__` as well: the two are kept in step by hand (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.__init__`).
`WSGIRequest.__init__` does not copy it: the request's `META` is that same dictionary, and the request also keeps it as `environ` (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`).

Django undoes the server's step and then decodes properly: `get_bytes_from_wsgi` encodes the string with ISO-8859-1, which gives back exactly the bytes the server had, and `get_path_info` decodes those as UTF-8, first percent-escaping any byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 so that the decoding cannot fail (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:get_bytes_from_wsgi`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:get_path_info`, `django/utils/encoding.py:repercent_broken_unicode`).

`get_script_name` takes the script name from `settings.FORCE_SCRIPT_NAME` when that is not `None`; otherwise from `"SCRIPT_URL"` or `"REDIRECT_URL"`, in which Apache's mod_rewrite leaves the URL as it was before rewriting, with the path info taken off its end, so that the script name is the one the client saw; and otherwise from the environ's `"SCRIPT_NAME"` (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:get_script_name`).
The constructor then writes the decoded script name and path info back into the environ, so `META` holds the corrected values (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`).
A `WSGIRequest` whose environ has no `"CONTENT_LENGTH"` therefore has an empty body (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:LimitedStream`).
A `WSGIRequest` whose environ has no `"CONTENT_LENGTH"` therefore has an empty body (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.__init__`, `django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:LimitedStream`).

By the time an `ASGIRequest` is made the handler has received the whole body into a temporary file, one that is held in memory until it grows past `settings.FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` and is then written to disk (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.read_body`), and the constructor is given the scope and that file ([The two entry points](../handlers/entry.md#an-asgi-request) has the handler's side).
The file becomes the request's stream as it is, with no wrapper (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).

WSGI's test is only that the setting is not `None`, so a setting of `""` forces an empty script name under WSGI and is passed over under ASGI (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:get_script_prefix`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).

The constructor therefore drops every header with an underscore in its name (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).
Under WSGI this is the server's affair, and Django's development server does the same before it builds the environ (`django/core/servers/basehttp.py:WSGIRequestHandler.get_environ`).
It now ignores such headers, as Daphne, the reference ASGI server, does (`docs/releases/6.0.4.txt`).

HTTP/2 lets a client send each cookie as a `"cookie"` header of its own, and a comma is not what separates cookies, so those values are joined with a semicolon and a space (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`).
If one of the parameters is a charset that Python has a codec for, it becomes the request's `encoding`; an unknown charset is ignored (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._set_content_type_params`).

A view or a middleware may assign it, and because the collections may already have been decoded with the old value, the setter deletes `GET` and the parsed `POST`, so that the next read parses them again (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.encoding`).

The setter leaves `FILES` alone, so it still holds the files of the first parse until `POST` is read again; that read comes back empty, and empties `FILES` with it (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest._load_post_and_files`).

`ASGIRequest.GET` does not: its constructor has decoded the scope's query string as UTF-8 to put it in `META`, and the `QueryDict` decodes the percent-escapes in it with the default charset, whatever the request's encoding is (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIRequest.GET`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.GET`).

It stores the new encoding, then asks whether the request has `GET`, and deletes it if so (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.encoding`).

The setter's parse of the query string raises `TooManyFieldsSent` from the constructor in the same way, when the query string has more parameters than `settings.DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_NUMBER_FIELDS` allows (`django/http/request.py:QueryDict.__init__`).

Under either handler, then, the exception reaches the server with no response made, and what the client sees is the server's doing (`django/core/handlers/wsgi.py:WSGIHandler.__call__`, `django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIHandler.create_request`).
